propositions: Pandoc 3.6.1 escapes arrows inside code spans, deletes HTML comments, and corrupts arrow delimiters; a two-phase lexer must lock code, comments, fences, and indented blocks, then classify by safety before rendering.

The renderer must classify units as pass-through (locked blocks, existing wiki), unambiguous wiki markers ({{…}}, [a|b], {color:}), ambiguous markers (*x*, _x_ only safe in pure prose), tables, HTML tags, regex-dangerous prose, or fallback to pandoc commonmark→jira with no monkeypatch.

Code fragments must be extracted before arrow substitution (→/←/↔/⇒) and preserved byte-identically in post-render output, else that unit falls back to original Markdown to mitigate unpredictable escaping.

A deterministic 178-body corpus (29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose) with pinned strata, rendered-body ratio ≥0.90 and rendered-character ratio ≥0.95, verifies coverage without silent corruption as the store grows.

pypandoc-binary==1.15 bundles pandoc 3.6.1; a non-skipping real-binary test gates Linux/macOS CI, Windows falls back to identity, and wiki tests hard-import to verify exact versions and jira writer behavior.

Missing pandoc returns exact body with wiki_render_fallback event (reason: pandoc_absent); conversion or preservation failures return exact unit with conversion_failure or preservation_failure reason, never logging bodies.
